files.outer.sh:
/usr/sbin/ip link set lo up || echo loopback-down
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_unprivileged_port_start || echo sysctl-failed
exec /usr/bin/unshare --user --map-user=2000 --map-group=2000 "$BASH" --noprofile --norc /tmp/parity-case/inner.sh
files.rsyncd.conf:
pid file = /tmp/parity-home/rsyncd.pid
log file = /tmp/parity-home/rsyncd.log
lock file = /tmp/parity-home/rsyncd.lock
port = 873
address = 127.0.0.1
use chroot = no
numeric ids = yes
max connections = 8
[mod]
    path = /tmp/parity-case/module
    read only = no
[ro]
    path = /tmp/parity-case/module-ro
    read only = yes
[denied]
    path = /tmp/parity-case/module-ro
    hosts deny = 127.0.0.1
files.inner.sh:
listening() { local _a l _r st _x
  while read -r _a l _r st _x; do [[ $l == 0100007F:$1 && $st == 0A ]] && return 0; done < /proc/net/tcp
  return 1; }
up() { local i
  for ((i = 0; i < 200; i++)); do
    listening "$1" && return 0
    kill -0 "$2" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    sleep 0.05
  done
  return 1; }
if [[ $BASH == /opt/bash-5.3.15/bin/bash ]]; then rs() { /usr/bin/rsync "$@"; }; else rs() { rsync "$@"; }; fi
/usr/bin/rsync --daemon --no-detach --config=/tmp/parity-case/rsyncd.conf </dev/null >/dev/null 2>>/tmp/parity-home/rsyncd.err & dpid=$!
up 0369 "$dpid" || echo daemon-not-listening
shopt -s globstar nullglob dotglob
tree() { local f; for f in "$1"/**; do if [ -d "$f" ]; then echo "dir:$f"; else echo "file:$f:$(<"$f")"; fi; done; }
rs -r src/ rsync://127.0.0.1:873/mod/pushed/ >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "push-rc=$?"
tree module
kill "$dpid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$dpid" 2>/dev/null
echo daemon-stopped

cases.stdout:
push-rc=0
dir:module/pushed
file:module/pushed/a.txt:alpha
dir:module/pushed/sub
file:module/pushed/sub/b.txt:beta
file:module/.keep:
daemon-stopped
ns-status=0
cases.oracle: GNU rsync 3.5.0 (Debian trixie; the original asks for 3.4) client and daemon in a private user+net namespace on 127.0.0.1:873; the reference side runs /usr/bin/rsync as client against the same daemon configuration, the candidate side its rsync builtin against that GNU daemon (candidate speaks protocol 27; the daemon accepts the downgrade).
cases.comparison: r1: pushing a two-file tree to rsync://127.0.0.1:873/mod/pushed/ transfers both files (with the nested directory) into the daemon module, status 0, and the module directory listing is identical on both sides
